questions: Does the 15 mm pitch keep at least one sensor on tape through the bends, or do all sensors drop out (line loss) before the robot recovers?
Did narrowing the track to 0.10 m give enough yaw authority to hold the centre line, or does the robot now overshoot and oscillate?
Is progress now limited by the drift off the line (ended_by off_track) or by speed (ended_by stall or time)?
If the robot still leaves the track, does max_error stay near 0.06 m on all tracks, which would point to a remaining lag or gain problem rather than sensor coverage?

intent: Widen the sensor bar from 10 mm to 15 mm pitch (+/-0.03 m span) so the line stays visible at larger offsets, and narrow the wheel track from 0.12 to 0.10 m to raise yaw response per unit of PWM. Mass drops to 0.7 kg to match. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and lower max_error, with completion in the development tracks becoming possible.
learning: Iteration 0 showed a steady drift off the line with few oscillations, which points to sensor coverage and turn authority rather than lag. Iteration 1 changes the sensor pitch and the track together, so the next race will show whether the coverage change alone is enough. If line_loss_events drop but progress stays low, the next step is to reduce the forward offset to 0.02 m or raise wheel_radius for top speed.
rationale: The iteration-0 race evidence (entityR2A) shows all 60 trials ended off_track on every development track, with progress of only 10 to 18 percent. The max_error of about 0.06 m sits on the off-track limit, and rms_error is about 0.03 m. Line_loss_events averaged 1 to 2 per run, and steering_oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.16). So the robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily off the line and loses it, and the line is lost only once it is already far from centre. The 5-sensor bar spans only +/-0.02 m. With a 12 mm footprint, all sensors go dark at a tape-centre offset of about 0.045 m, which is close to the 0.06 m limit and leaves almost no recovery margin. I therefore widen the bar to 15 mm pitch, spanning +/-0.03 m. This keeps the tape visible to the sensors at larger offsets, so the signal does not drop out before the controller can respond. Second, the drift could partly reflect weak turn authority. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so narrowing the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m gives more yaw per unit of PWM command. I also lower mass to 0.7 kg to reduce yaw inertia. I keep the forward offset at 0.04 m and the footprint at 12 mm so that the two changes can be attributed separately. The wheel radius stays at 0.03 m. Expected result: fewer line_loss_events, lower max_error, and progress above 0.5 on the oval and s-bend. The next race will show whether the pitch change or the track change does most of the work.
